definitions.rule: PASS if s < t_low; REVIEW if t_low <= s < t_high; FAIL if s >= t_high

training.loop: PyTorch loop around Ultralytics yolo11n-cls with Ultralytics transforms; AdamW, linear warm-up then cosine decay; checkpoint + auto-resume

assumption_notes.c_fp: Anchored on Cheshire East's GBP 8.47 per km per gritting run (operational) and Norfolk's ~GBP 49,000 per full run over 49 routes (~GBP 1,000 per ~72 km route). A ~10 km spot treatment plus ~20 km deadhead => roughly EUR 300-500; EUR 400 used. Scenario estimate.
assumption_notes.c_fn: Scenario build-up for ONE decision cycle (1 h; the next hourly check is a new case, so longer exposure is not double counted): 10 km segment x 600 veh/h = 6,000 veh-km; +3 crashes per million veh-km when snow/slush is untreated (between the ~+20% injury-crash effect of reduced salting in Finland and the ~8x before/after-salting ratio in Kuemmel & Hanbali 1992) => 0.018 crashes x EUR 40,000 average crash (EU external-cost handbook injury values mixed with property-damage-only crashes) = EUR 720; + ~EUR 150 delay (FHWA: arterial speeds fall 30-40% on snowy/slushy pavement); + ~EUR 130 extra de-icing once snow is compacted. Total ~EUR 1,000. Most uncertain number; see sensitivity and break-even.
assumption_notes.prevalence: Scenario assumption for winter-season operations; the dataset is ~71% snow/slush, which is curated, not a production rate.
assumption_notes.cases_per_day: Scenario: 60 hot-spot cameras checked hourly, 24 h/day in winter.
assumption_notes.review_seconds: Scenario: open the image, glance at the neighbouring camera and pavement sensor.
assumption_notes.reviewer_hourly_cost: Eurostat 2024 average hourly labour cost EUR 37.3 (euro area), rounded up for 24/7 shift premia.
assumption_notes.productive_hours_per_reviewer_day: Scenario: 6 of 8 shift hours available for reviewing.
assumption_notes.review_capacity_hours_per_day: Scenario: three 8 h duty-officer shifts can each spare ~2 h.
assumption_notes.reviewer_error: Scenario: 5% miss / 5% false alarm; perfect (0/0) and 10/10 tested as alternatives.

zero_shot_multiclass_note: ImageNet has no Clear/Wet/Slush/Snow classes; multiclass zero-shot accuracy is undefined. It is scored only at case level via the stated snow-class mapping.

coco_zero_shot.mapping_used: Stated a priori: FAIL if a 'skis' or 'snowboard' box with conf >= 0.25 is detected, else PASS. These classes describe winter sports, not road surfaces, so the mapping is weak by construction; it is reported only to show the detector's operational behaviour.
